taxonomyNote: NatureServe places North American treefrogs in Dryophytes (Duellman et al. 2016); ADW and the batch list use Hyla. NatureServe name: Dryophytes versicolor.
fieldMarks: 3-5 cm (record 6 cm); warty skin, usually gray with black back blotches, or green, brown or pearl-gray; colour changes with background, season and humidity.
Orange to golden-yellow, black-speckled concealed hindleg surfaces; white belly.
Identical to Cope's gray treefrog; call is a slower, more musical trill.
behavior: Most active at dusk and at night, especially in wet weather; inactive from fall through early spring.
Males are territorial when calling; adults may eat smaller gray treefrogs.
Migrates up to several hundred metres to breeding pools; breeds spring or summer (usually May in the north); larvae metamorphose within 2 months.
habitat: Wooded and forested habitats on the ground, shrubs or trees; rests in tree holes, under bark or in rotten logs; breeds in still shallow woodland ponds, marshes, puddles and swamps.
range: Southeastern Canada from southern Manitoba to New Brunswick, south through the northeastern and south-central US to North Carolina, West Virginia, Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky, Illinois, Tennessee, eastern Texas and southwestern Louisiana, west to North Dakota, Minnesota, Iowa, eastern Kansas and eastern Oklahoma.

lookalikes.name: Cope's gray treefrog
lookalikes.howToTell: Indistinguishable by sight; faster, higher-pitched trill.
